justifications.c1: Fines cited (Ling £15,858 + £3,858, search-confirmed; £15k; £4k) are for contractors not providing welfare at all; researcher found no cost for a mid-week overflow or run-dry, an emergency call-out or lost hire revenue.
justifications.c2: Weekly emptying is the planning norm (BS 6465-1 via BSG, attribution uncertain) and hire firms service weekly (vendor); the claimed between-visit overflow/run-dry events have no frequency data.
justifications.c3: Weekly servicing within hire price and separately bookable waste-tank emptying (Site Equip, vendor), fixed-route driver jobs (Pertemps, YoungCapital); cost per visit not evidenced in the file.
justifications.c4: CDM 2015 Schedule 2 / Reg 13(4)(c) welfare duty with HSE prosecutions and improvement notices (Ling, Rochdale, Cheshire), but the duty sits with the principal contractor and nothing requires tank-level or service records.
justifications.c5: GAP Group 'Operations Manager, Tanker Services' advert and service operatives reporting to an Operations Manager identify the hire-firm buyer; no telematics budget evidenced.
justifications.c6: The hire firm's own drivers visit every unit weekly, so buyer and installer coincide; no evidence UK hirers or unit makers (AJC, Garic, Boss, Groundhog) sell telemetry.
justifications.c7: Sensoneo and Satellite Sense sell portable-toilet fill sensors and Enevo sells fill-level routing, but no prices or customer counts; the UK welfare-unit gap is asserted.
justifications.c8: Off-the-shelf ultrasonic level sensors cost £243-£511 each (Innon, Tekelek) and several sensors per unit are proposed, so BOM is well above £50 unless custom; waste-tank environment is harsh.
justifications.c9: Telemetry fee could ride the weekly hire line (£275-£325/week, Euroloo search-confirmed), but no record-keeping duty and no evidence anyone pays for service records.
justifications.c10: HSE press releases and trade press on welfare prosecutions and BSG breach statistics (third-party host, search-confirmed but uncorroborated), but nothing about hired units overflowing or running dry between services.

weakest: The specific failure targeted (a hired unit's tank filling or running dry between weekly services) has no evidence of frequency or cost; the prosecutions found are for not providing welfare at all.
